# spotlight_secret (Resource)

A secret that Spotlight injects into requests, for the hosts it is bound to. Spotlight stores its value and never returns it, so the value is write-only and never enters the plan or the state. Writing secrets needs a token granted the `secrets` scope. Import it as `<workspace id>/<name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "secret_linear_api_key" {
  description = "The value of the secret LINEAR_API_KEY, which Spotlight stores and never returns"
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "secret_google_maps_key" {
  description = "The value of the secret GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY, which Spotlight stores and never returns"
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

# Spotlight stores the value. The value is write-only. Terraform sends it when
# it creates the secret and when value_wo_version changes. The plan and the
# state never store it.
resource "spotlight_secret" "linear_api_key" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  name         = "LINEAR_API_KEY"
  bindings = [
    { host = "api.linear.app", prefix = "Bearer " },
  ]
  value_wo         = var.secret_linear_api_key
  value_wo_version = 1
}

# Spotlight puts this secret in the key query parameter. Use this for an API
# that takes its key in the URL.
resource "spotlight_secret" "google_maps_key" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  name         = "GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY"
  bindings = [
    { host = "maps.googleapis.com", location = "query", name = "key" },
  ]
  value_wo         = var.secret_google_maps_key
  value_wo_version = 1
}

# Terraform does not set this value. A person sets it on the Secrets settings
# page or with spotlight secret set LINEAR_SIGNING. Until then, a run that
# needs the secret does not start.
resource "spotlight_secret" "linear_signing" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  name         = "LINEAR_SIGNING"
}

# Terraform reads this value from AWS Secrets Manager. The value never enters
# the plan or the state. Change value_wo_version after you rotate the value in
# AWS, so Terraform sends the new value.
ephemeral "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "sentry_auth_token" {
  secret_id = "sentry/auth-token"
}

resource "spotlight_secret" "sentry_auth_token" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  name         = "SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN"
  bindings = [
    { host = "sentry.io", prefix = "Bearer " },
  ]
  value_wo         = ephemeral.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.sentry_auth_token.secret_string
  value_wo_version = 1
}

# A harness profile can give this value to its runs as an environment
# variable, through its env. The agent and every process in the sandbox can
# read it, so use this only for a value made for the sandbox, such as a
# development key.
resource "spotlight_secret" "dev_github_app_key" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  name         = "DEV_GITHUB_APP_KEY"
  sandbox      = "env"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) What integrations call the secret, as in `LINEAR_API_KEY`, written `secret.LINEAR_API_KEY` where an integration or a harness profile names it. It is immutable, so changing it replaces the secret.
- `workspace_id` (String) The workspace the secret belongs to. Changing it replaces the secret.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `bindings` (Attributes List) The only hosts the secret is ever sent to, and where Spotlight injects it there; a request anywhere else goes without it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings))
- `sandbox` (String) Whether a run can get the value itself. `stand-in` (the default) keeps the value out of every sandbox, and egress puts it only in the requests to the bound hosts. `env` lets a harness profile give the value to its runs as an environment variable, through its `env`, where the agent and every process in the sandbox can read it. A secret cannot go back to `stand-in` while a harness profile names it in `env`.
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The value Spotlight stores, usually read from a sensitive variable. Leave it and `value_wo_version` out to set the value in the app or with `spotlight secret set` instead; removing both keeps the stored value until a person replaces it. It is sent to Spotlight and never stored in the plan or the state, so it needs Terraform 1.11 or later; change `value_wo_version` to send it again.
- `value_wo_version` (Number) Any number, set exactly when `value_wo` is set; change it whenever `value_wo` changes, so Terraform sends the new value.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Names the resource within its workspace, as in `LINEAR_API_KEY`.
- `id` (String) Issued by Spotlight when the secret is created, and never changed.
- `rotated_at` (String) When Spotlight last took a new value.
- `version` (Number) Rises with every change to the secret; each write sends it back so a change made since is not overwritten.

<a id="nestedatt--bindings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings`

Required:

- `host` (String) The host, as in `api.linear.app`, with no scheme, port or path. The secret goes there over HTTPS only.

Optional:

- `location` (String) Whether Spotlight injects the secret in a request header or in a query parameter: `header` (the default) or `query`.
- `name` (String) The header or query parameter that Spotlight injects the secret in. A header defaults to `authorization`; Spotlight stores a header name in lower case. A query parameter must be named.
- `prefix` (String) The text that Spotlight writes before the value, as in `Bearer `.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_secret.linear_api_key
  identity = {
    id = "3f8a1c2e-6b4d-4e7a-9c1f-0d2b5e8a7c63"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The id Spotlight issued the secret when it was created.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_secret.linear_api_key
  id = "5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/LINEAR_API_KEY"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a secret with the id of its workspace and its name.
terraform import spotlight_secret.linear_api_key 5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/LINEAR_API_KEY
```
